reason: The five paired-load proposals are the same core experiment. I rank the n=512 version first because it confines the change to full tiles and has a locally verified SME2 instruction form; the supplied incumbent assembly still shows four separate loads. This supports testing code generation and correctness, not a speedup. Indirect ZA row transfer ranks next because supplied probe evidence confirms its code shape and sample correctness, with external GEMM evidence only as motivation. The remaining proposals test distinct packing, transpose, streaming-region, or scheduling changes, but have no hill timing evidence and carry more implementation or correctness risk. Fresh baseline scores vary widely, and historical candidate results do not establish gains or causes. `cache_blocking` duplicates the paired-load proposal, so it ranks last to favor distinct evidence.
